classification.difficultyReason: Sketch translated downward-opening parabolas using their vertices and calculated y-intercepts.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of the following, labelling the $y$-intercept and vertex.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=-x^2$ down 7 units. The vertex is $(0,-7)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$.

When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-0^2-7\\y&=-7\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,-7)$. Sketch a downward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Downward parabola with coincident vertex and y-intercept labelled.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=-x^2$ up 7 units. The vertex is $(0,7)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$.

When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-0^2+7\\y&=7\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,7)$. Sketch a downward-opening parabola.

spec.description: Downward parabola crossing the x-axis twice; coincident vertex and y-intercept labelled.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=-x^2$ right 3 units and up 5 units. The vertex is $(3,5)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=3$.

When $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0-3)^2+5\\y&=-9+5\\y&=-4\end{align*}$$
Label $(0,-4)$ and $(3,5)$ on the downward-opening sketch.

spec.description: Downward parabola with vertex and y-intercept labelled.
